# Project MyoSuite Task and Independent Native Replay

Issue #11983 implements an explicitly project-defined task using the actual
MyoSuite 3.0.0 `MyoGymnasiumEnv` lifecycle on MuJoCo 3.6.0. It is not an
official supplied golf benchmark. The independent physics executor retains
its MuJoCo identity, separately from the MyoSuite inventory correspondence.
All six ecosystems and all 17 required model/variant rows remain required.

## Model, State, and Action Semantics

`myosuite_project_task_producer.py` loads the original MJCF path with its
relative resource layout. The SDK performs reset, action clipping, one native
step and forward realization, observation construction and reward bookkeeping.
The project observations contain native configuration, velocity and activation;
the constant bookkeeping reward is not a motion-matching score. The original
model defines units, frames, actuator order, dynamics, timestep and integrator.
This integration does not recalibrate anatomy or contact.

For action $c_k$, the recorded command is the actual native control readback
$u_k=\operatorname{clip}(c_k,\ell,h)$. Compiled limited channels retain their
finite bounds. Unlimited channels use infinite action bounds; unused native
`ctrlrange` entries are not zero limits. The production driver and iron have
14 motor and 86 muscle channels, 100 commands and 86 activations. Their inputs
remain mixed `ACTUATOR_COMMAND`, not generalized torques or pure excitation.

The state $S_k$ is the complete native `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` vector, including
native time, configuration, velocity, activation, controls and numerical
history. It is read after the SDK's native forward realization. Record
$N$ commands with $N+1$ state/time samples. The exporter repeats the last command
once as the T01 ZOH terminal boundary value; the executor integrates only the
first $N$ commands. No terminal step is invented.

## Clock and Restart Policy

Initialization policy `mujoco-integration-state-restore-forward` version 1.1.0
restores the complete hashed native state and derives its actual native clock
origin $t_0$ from `data.time`. T01 time remains simulation-relative:

$$\tau_k=t_k-t_0,\qquad t_k=t_0+\tau_k.$$

Native state rows retain absolute epochs. Returned replay timestamps are
measured elapsed times, not the requested grid substituted into output. Initial
forward realization must preserve time exactly. Version 1.0.0 retains its
zero-native-origin restriction. Nonzero applied external forces remain forbidden
in this native-own-contact pathway.

Every observed interval must be finite, strictly positive and satisfy

$$|\Delta t-\delta|\leq
\max(10^{-9}\delta,64\operatorname{ulp}(\delta)),\qquad
\text{tolerance}<\delta/2.$$

This is the existing T04 numerical clock precision policy, not an experimental
physical acceptance threshold. It uses neither absolute-epoch ULPs nor a
completed-step count. Elapsed-horizon agreement is checked separately. Large
finite epochs that stall or materially distort a native step fail admission.
Suffix replay restores $S_j$ and applies $u_j$ next, preserving the original
boundary state's prior control until that input is applied.

## Interchange, Verification, and Provenance

`project_task_replay_artifacts.py` builds the existing Tools T01 replay bundle
and compiled-actuator profile. `native_direct_model_provider.py` creates a fresh
native model/data pair with no SDK step, reset, observation or reward methods.
`native_direct_model_replay.py` owns the existing independent stepping loop.
No second replay format or physics engine is introduced.

Source entry-point and resource-closure bytes are frozen before SDK model
construction and checked after loading, around recording and at export.
Rehashed comments or whitespace that leave the compiled MJB unchanged still
fail original-source admission. A post-hoc equivalent compilation cannot prove
the exact source bytes that produced a history.

The freezer admits SDK/task/source identity, complete finite dimensions,
state-clock consistency, native control bounds and the original transitive
include/mesh/texture closure. It compiles that closure against the producer's
executed MJB digest. The existing direct executor then independently verifies
every claimed state, command and elapsed time before artifacts are returned.
This adds one linear native replay to export; it does not rerun an optimizer.

SDK version/base source and project source are retained separately from the
native replay provider, binary/runtime, compiled model, resource closure,
ordered actuator laws, state/input schemas, initial-state digest and profile.
Method replacement checks are misuse guards. Integrity records are not
signatures; caller-supplied provenance requires independent lineage verification.
The exact reviewed SDK base-source SHA-256 is
`53ad8bc71fc07a2e7fcead164ca027a33418b9ac1aa953ea6c4042fa48eed154`.
An actual reset/step execution profile identified the CPU accessor in that
same file and the concrete `envs/muscle_stages.py` helper. Its reviewed digest
is `eb2d5af2b2c4e842626aa3b29eb1a9c77c93a62a4650a6a50bda492832d3b107`;
distribution METADATA is separately bound to
`39e5fbbea88bb4aa29c42fc1d13f5846877b179094402d7c80e839f25ceb9698`.
This is a bounded execution-source audit, not recursive package attestation.

MuJoCo 3.6.0 and 3.8.0 use exact reviewed required actuator field sets.
Only 3.6 omits its nonexistent `actuator_armature`, `actuator_damping` and
`actuator_dampingpoly` fields. Missing required fields and unknown versions fail;
absent values are never manufactured. Shared schema identity does not imply
that different native runtimes or compiled models are physically interchangeable.

### Model Fingerprint Scratch Ownership

Every pre-step and post-step compiled-model check remains in place. Recording
owns one writable, contiguous, one-dimensional `uint8` scratch array of exactly
the current native serialized-model size. It zeros the array before every save
and hashes its memory view immediately after serialization. Scratch is neither
shared across runs nor retained in history. The optional buffer rejects invalid
storage instead of silently copying it. This preserves zero-padding semantics
and avoids repeated allocation and the extra bytes copy.

A production-driver serialization microbenchmark on MuJoCo 3.6 used a
29,487,449-byte model. Twenty original allocation/save/copy/hash operations took
0.9078 s; twenty zero-fill/save/view/hash operations took 0.5152 s, with identical
digests throughout. This measures fingerprint overhead only. It does not
establish full-rollout or optimization speed. Native regression checks compare
prefilled scratch against external MJB bytes and detect model-mass changes.

## Evidence and Reproduction

The 2026-10-09 actual MyoSuite 3.0.0/MuJoCo 3.6.0 campaign passed 70 tests with
zero skips, including both unchanged production resource closures, T01 reload,
complete-state uninterrupted/suffix/changed-future replay, real SDK lifecycle,
mixed control mapping, poisoned SDK hooks during independent replay, source and
law/channel mutations, malformed histories, unexecuted transitions and large
epoch clock failures. Earlier RED attempts are retained. Separate MuJoCo 3.8
regression evidence is 44 passes and three explicitly unavailable fixture or
environment skips; it is not substituted for the actual SDK runtime.
After the exporter architecture refactor and scratch optimization, the current
actual SDK campaign passed 76 tests with zero failures, errors or skips. This
includes six buffer-equivalence, mutation and storage-contract regressions in
addition to the original integration/adversarial cases.

Run with the reviewed actual SDK/native pair, exact Tools pin and retained
complete public production resource root:

```powershell
$env:FEEDBACK_MYOSUITE_PRODUCTION_ROOT = '<complete-myosuite-resource-root>'
python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts= `
  tests/unit/engines/myosuite/test_project_task_producer.py `
  tests/unit/engines/myosuite/test_project_task_artifact_admission.py `
  tests/unit/engines/myosuite/test_native_model_resource_closure.py `
  --junitxml='<retained-attempt-path>.xml'
```

The production positive is a three-step numerical integration probe, with
nonzero activation and velocity and nonconstant mixed commands. Its suffix and
changed future are correspondingly short. This is not a full-capture fit,
physiological force validation, convergence study, muscle-only assistance
qualification or parity completion. Complete capture horizon, calibration,
anatomy, contact/grip and fully muscle-driven OpenSim acceptance remain open.

A separate nominal viability experiment completed 1,814 driver and 1,828 iron
native steps, spanning the respective capture durations, using zero motor
commands and constant 0.05 muscle commands. Both original producer runs had no
native warnings and exact complete-state, command and clock replay through the
serialized T01 pathway. These were executed with the original producer, before
the scratch-buffer optimization. They use capture duration only and contain no
feedback fit. Maximum observed contact penetration was about 0.0317 m; the
maximum absolute native constraint residual was about 1.0498 in mixed native
units and must not be interpreted as a distance or an accepted equality error.
These diagnostics preserve the unresolved contact/constraint readiness gate.

### Initial Assembly and Support Admission

Read-only native forward evaluation of all 1,815 driver and 1,829 iron saved
states located the largest weld residual at reset, before the later collapse.
Both saved reset poses exactly equal compiled `qpos0`. Right and left
hand-to-club grip-site origins start about 1.1703 m and 0.9940 m apart, with
active site welds. MuJoCo permits site welds to start separated and align during
simulation ([MuJoCo 3.6 weld reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.6.0/XMLreference.html#equality-weld)).
This identifies an initial-assembly admission concern; it does not prove a
defective source model or an infeasible assembled pose.

The auxiliary foot welds join bodies with declared relative poses. Their
body-origin separation is not a weld error, and collision-disabled auxiliary
spheres do not establish floor support. Native `ncon` is zero at reset. Later
maximum penetration is skull against the included scene's cylinder platform,
approximately 0.0317 m, distinct from the named floor plane. Site-frame closure,
body-weld relative pose, joint limits and named physical contact pairs require
separate units and acceptance criteria. One mixed `efc_pos` norm cannot qualify
all of them.

Before controller fitting, freeze an explicit initial-pose and support policy.
Preserve the original complete state and distinguish `source_default`,
`reference_derived` and `optimizer_assembled` provenance. Assembly must use
bounded native tangent-space motion on the unchanged compiled model, retain
source ranges and equality activation, and independently reload complete
integration state before checking grip closure, joint feasibility, support
identity, penetration and allowed displacement. An assembled pose alone does
not prove capture correspondence or dynamic force balance. No qualified
MyoSuite capture-marker map or assembled production initial state is
demonstrated by the present nominal experiment.

Diagnostic scripts rechecked entry XML, compiled MJB and saved-history hashes;
they did not independently revalidate the entire transitive resource closure.
The observed Desk scene bytes differ from local scene bytes. The producer's
separate full resource-closure evidence remains separate. Desktop previews
restore saved states and render without integration, labeled **No Mocap Fit**.

## Owned Current-State SDK Forecasts

F09k (#12009) supplies `ProjectTaskForecaster` as a reusable shooting primitive.
Construction creates a distinct SDK task from the same original source closure
and requires an identical compiled native model. The live task's native handles,
source/resource lineage and SDK bindings remain pinned. Each prediction accepts
an observation whose complete integration state and individual native fields
exactly match the current live plant. Matching values establish consistency,
not authenticated snapshot origin; sample index remains caller bookkeeping.

Command conversion occurs inside a live-state guard. Recheck before any owned
execution, then SDK-reset only the owned task, restore every
`mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` field, call native forward preparation and verify exact
readback. This includes the absolute epoch, activation, controls and warmstart.
The existing SDK recorder executes the candidate and returns its existing
producer history. Native contacts and actuator laws remain those of the source
model. Independent export and replay still require the existing T01/profile
admission and native executor; a forecast is not replay qualification.

Reuse the existing replay restoration/admission check before any owned execution:
nonzero applied external loads are refused, and native callbacks/plugins retain
their existing restrictions. Astra's external-load review produced two actual
SDK RED regressions before repair. The final MyoSuite 3.0/MuJoCo 3.6 combined
campaign passes 109 cases, zero failures/errors/skips, including unchanged
production driver/iron suffix forecasts with exact full-state independent replay.
All twelve executed source/test hashes match. Retained source-bound evidence is
listed in F09k turnover. Two-step production predictions do not establish a
fitted capture, stable stance or physiological validity.

Every attempt checks the live state, model/source identity and global callback
policy on exit, including failures. No successful partial history is returned.
The forecaster detects caller mutation without rollback. A nonblocking ownership
lock rejects concurrent/reentrant use. Idempotent close releases only the owned
task; constructor failures after the owned factory returns also close it. The
factory's own pre-return failures remain governed by its existing implementation.
The forecast adapter has a separate guarded source digest.

`construction_seconds` measures allocation/admission; `last_attempt_seconds`
includes prediction admission, conversion, restoration, stepping and final
live validation, including failed attempts. Independent replay has its own cost.
No online deadline, optimizer, fitted control gains or production speedup is
established. Perfect-state prediction is distinct from state estimation and
robustness to model error or delayed measurements. Retain uncertainty and
capture-calibration requirements before promoting any tracking result.

## State-Dependent SDK Feedback Recording

F09j (#12003) adds a feedback input source to the same admitted SDK recording
loop. At sample k the policy receives immutable copied native-order qpos, qvel,
activation, control and complete integration state, plus absolute native time
and ordered actuator IDs. It receives no simulator handle. qpos and tangent
velocity dimensions remain distinct. The policy computes the next ordered
command; existing native bounds and SDK mapping determine the applied input.
The recorder retains N actual inputs and N+1 complete states.

Before integration, reject changed plant state, model fingerprints, SDK methods,
global callbacks, changed declared policy source and malformed/nonfinite actions.
Numeric command conversion occurs inside the callback guard, so a custom array
conversion cannot mutate the plant after validation. Policy exceptions propagate
without a successful partial recording; completed native steps remain and no
rollback or retry is implied. The fixed
action-table interface retains its pre-execution whole-table validation. Both
interfaces use one stepping loop and the same state/clock/source admission.

The feedback recording carries declared controller name/version, source-file
digest, caller-declared parameter digest and feedback-adapter source digest.
Separate `initial_state_array_sha256` and `applied_command_array_sha256` fields
hash raw array bytes; these are not the schema/channel/clock-bound T01 digests.
Preserve that provenance alongside the existing command history and
exported T01 artifacts. It is not a new replay format or a signature; source
guards do not attest hidden dependencies, mutable controller parameters or the
truth of caller declarations. Native provider identity stays separate from
controller identity. Independent replay consumes only the frozen state and
applied commands and does not invoke feedback or SDK lifecycle hooks.

The actual MyoSuite 3.0/MuJoCo 3.6 combined campaign passed 89 tests with zero
skips, including thirteen feedback/snapshot/adversarial tests and the prior 76
integration/resource cases. A four-step native fixture used velocity feedback
to produce changing motor commands and independently reproduced every complete
state. An actual native regression first reproduced a deferred-conversion state
mutation, then passed after conversion moved inside the guard. A second-call
exception test verifies exactly one completed step and no successful record.
This is neither learned control tuning nor production pose, capture-fit,
physiology, muscle-only actuation or all-model qualification. Initial assembly,
qualified observation mapping and whole-horizon controller optimization remain
required before the muscular OpenSim endpoint can be accepted.

## Provisional Persistent Native Search and Guarded Promotion

F09l (#12014) adds `ProjectTaskNativeSearch` beside the owned SDK forecaster.
Allocate a separately owned original-source native context from a genuinely
frozen, independently verified seed. Reuse the existing direct-command kernel;
there is no alternate integration loop or weakened SDK recording mode.
Each candidate starts from the complete current live integration state and an
explicit finite horizon bounded by `max_steps`. Inputs are ordered post-mapping
native controls. Native control limits are enforced without implicit clamping.
Unsupported applied external loads are refused before owned restoration.

Source, compiled-model, live-state, adapter and callback checks surround every
attempt. Owned model fingerprints are checked at invocation boundaries, rather
than the SDK producer's per-step model checks. Consequently every returned
trajectory and ranking is provisional. Immutable arrays accompany the existing
genuine T01 planned bundle, retaining model/provider, current initial state,
channel, clock, policy and input identity. This is a planned input artifact;
it does not qualify the candidate trajectory or establish execution.

`promote` accepts commands alone. Recompute the entire plan through the guarded
SDK forecast, require exact applied-command correspondence, and evaluate both
caller numerical callbacks on bytes-backed immutable history arrays. Hard
criteria must return the Boolean `True`, and the objective must be finite.
Existing export verifies complete transitions with an independent native model;
its canonical admission serializes and reloads T01 before replay. A poisoned
provisional state or score cannot supply the promoted objective. Callbacks can
still depend on undeclared external data: their returned scalar is a numerical
result, not authenticated scientific scoring. The optimizer layer must bind
reference, scales, objective and hard-criterion provenance independently.

A validated future plan is distinct from the live executed prefix. Search and
promotion never reset or step the live task. Owned reset clears only owned
warning/history state; full state readback includes nonzero epoch, activation,
controls and warmstart. Reject reentrancy and stale snapshots. Preserve
failure→A recovery even after a real owned step has completed. Idempotent
closure releases only the search context; the caller retains its forecaster.

Actual SDK API-absence RED contains seven failures. The first native GREEN has
seven passes in 23.22 seconds. Astra then identified writable owning arrays at
the promotion callback boundary; two actual regressions failed before the
immutable-copy fix. The subsequent twelve-case campaign passed in 28.89 seconds.
These are distinct historical checkpoints, not a claim that later expanded
source is covered by earlier receipts. Retain final combined JUnit and all
executed source/test hashes as specified in F09l turnover.

The final expanded actual SDK campaign passes 130 cases with zero failures,
errors or skips in 126.06 seconds. All fourteen executed source/test hashes
match. This includes both unchanged original production driver/iron models:
twenty-step A→B→A search histories exactly match the guarded SDK full histories,
and promotion independently replays every state, command and clock. Separate
partial-owned-execution failure recovery also matches every guarded state row.
The numerical finite-state criterion in those production tests establishes no
contact/constraint feasibility, fitted motion or physiological acceptance.

`construction_seconds`, `last_attempt_seconds` and plan `validation_seconds`
include their admission/final-guard overhead and failed attempts. A separate
unchanged-source twenty-step prototype measured four full histories exactly
equal to guarded SDK histories: persistent native attempts took approximately
0.45–0.51 seconds and guarded forecasts 2.49–2.66 seconds. These uncontrolled
diagnostics do not establish a general speedup, real-time operation or an
accepted optimizer. Full capture, calibrated markers/ground, contact/grip,
physiological validity, all seventeen model rows and six ecosystems remain
required, with muscular OpenSim and full-horizon independent excitation replay
as the final endpoint.

## Frozen Native Tracking Objective

`myosuite_project_tracking.py` adds frozen native reference and physical-scale
objects plus a source-bound `ProjectTaskTrackingObjective`. It uses owned scratch
MjData and native `mj_differentiatePos` to compare positions on the configuration
manifold. It never forwards, integrates, resets or commands the live task.
Velocity residuals compare native qvel coordinates without transporting twists.
Activation and exact post-mapping command increments retain native units.
Positive physical scales make each squared residual dimensionless. These costs
are discrete sums on one frozen grid, not timestep-invariant integrals. Slew
cost is a soft penalty; the optimizer must separately enforce hard slew bounds.

Freeze absolute reference clocks, reference provenance declaration, all scales,
complete initial integration state, previous native controls, ordered actuators,
compiled/source/resource-closure identities and implementation hashes. Reject
changed parameters, live anchors, clocks, command bounds and model/source/SDK/
producer lineage. Preserve bytes-backed immutable reference arrays. A digest
binds a declaration; it does not authenticate anatomy, measured subject identity
or arbitrary provisional arrays. Callers serialize live task mutation.

Use the same scorer for provisional native predictions and fully guarded SDK
histories. `history_cost` is admissible as the existing promotion objective:
source/full-state live guards can nest, while the scorer owns its own scratch
lock. Guarded promotion recomputes commands and independently replays complete
serialized/reloaded T01 histories. Numerical costs cannot override hard physical
admission. A validated future plan is separate from an executed live prefix.

Actual API-absence RED contains ten failures; first native GREEN has ten passes
in 18.92 seconds. Two additional genuine lineage regressions fail before their
checks are added. The expanded sixteen-case actual SDK campaign passes in
56.23 seconds, including both unchanged original production golfer models and
full twenty-step guarded promotion plus independent replay. These tests use
hold references and finite-state admission, not private-capture physical gates.
See F09m turnover for final combined evidence and bounded-search integration.
The final seven-module actual SDK campaign passes 146 tests with zero failures,
errors or skips in 179.14 seconds; all sixteen executed source/test hashes match.
All seventeen production rows, six ecosystems and muscular OpenSim remain open.

## Bounded Native Command Solve With Guarded Fallback

F09n (#12036) connects the native predictor and frozen tracking objective to
the shared F02 bounded candidate search. `NativeCommandSolveProblem` freezes
ordered post-mapping initial/fallback plans, channel bounds, per-sample command
increments and a caller-declared hard-criteria provenance digest. Parameter
and callback-identity checks reject changed solve declarations. The digest is
an integrity binding of a declaration, not physiological authentication.

For each native sample, require lower and upper command bounds and
`abs(c[k]-c[k-1]) <= increment`, with `c[-1]` equal to the actual observed
previous control. These are applied-command constraints, not coefficient bounds
or continuous rates. Require explicit nonempty finite complete-state signed
margins throughout the horizon. Their physical laws, units and tolerances are
model-specific caller obligations; dummy finite-state fixture margins cannot
admit native contact or physiology. The shared optimizer's numerical feasibility
tolerance does not relax the exact guarded command/increment checks.

Promote and independently replay the full fallback before numerical search.
Numerical success proposes commands only. Recompute selected commands through
the guarded SDK history, recompute full-horizon hard criteria and objective,
and independently replay the existing serialized/reloaded T01 artifact.
Require improvement over the guarded fallback cost. Rejection, cancellation or
budget expiry retains the admitted fallback; changed live anchor, source,
identity or solve parameters cause failure. No live command is applied here.
Future prefix execution still requires current-state admission.

The receipt measures fallback, search and promotion overhead within this solve.
Complete time-to-accepted-match also includes external preparation, model/provider
construction, reference mapping, failed solves and export. Cooperative budgets
cannot establish a hard real-time guarantee, and native contact smoothness is
not assumed for SLSQP. The synthetic motor/activation fixture demonstrates a
real numerical improvement and guarded replay; it does not qualify a private
swing, production hard margins, muscle physiology or full-model parity.
Current-source evidence and remaining integration gates are recorded in F09n
turnover. All seventeen model rows, six ecosystems and muscular OpenSim remain
required.

The final affected actual MyoSuite 3.0/MuJoCo 3.6 campaign passes 170 tests with
zero failures/errors/skips in 250.31 seconds. Twenty executed source/test hashes
match before/after and the current worktree. In the synthetic three-step case,
the objective falls from 16.3614474 to 0.000299930 in 189 numerical evaluations;
whole solve elapsed time is 44.93 seconds. This establishes a correct numerical
baseline and a measured performance bottleneck, not rapid matching. Profile
native guard/prediction work and derivative strategy under the same source,
state and physical admission requirements before claiming production speed.

## Admitted Dependency and Private Contract Integration

F09o (#12044) integrates the admitted F01b/Tools-main source and private replay
consumer migration into the native solve stack. The consumed Tools revision is
`86d0f28b1cc5acf61185e07e320c816c2d005512`; Python requirements, Rust dependency
and gitlink must agree. Native replay contracts load through the existing
`load_pinned_tools_package` seam into one private module/class identity, without
grafting the vendor package into UpstreamDrift's public namespace. This changes
executed provider lineage and requires fresh actual-SDK replay evidence.

Preserve previous source/pin-specific receipts. Acceptance metadata advances
only after actual capability probes and served-artifact verification at the
new dependency. Native source/runtime hashes and affected admission/forecast/
tracking/solve tests must be rechecked together. Neither a pin update nor an
import identity check establishes capture correspondence, hard-contact validity,
muscle physiology, rapid matching or all-model parity. See the F09o plan and
turnover for exact executed evidence and remaining gates.
